topIssues.title: Green CI does not mean tested — advisory coverage + vacuous-green runner holes swallow failures
topIssues.author: lalalune
topIssues.body:
## Context

Green CI does not mean the change is tested. Two layers fail open.

### Coverage enforcement is advisory (re-opens the core of closed #9943/#8801)

- `lint-lane-coverage.mjs` runs `--dry-run` warn-only (`.github/workflows/ci.yaml:150-154`) and `ci.yaml` triggers on `[main]` only (`:9-12`), so it doesn't even run on develop PRs. Live state: **160 blocking issues, 104/146 plugins missing deterministic E2E/scenario coverage**, all suppressed by `--dry-run`; `lint-lane-coverage.allowlist.json` doesn't exist.
- `coverage-gate.yml` is the only per-change coverage gate and is structurally narrow: it runs only when a **changed test file** exists (`:6-8`,`:88-91`) — a PR adding new source with no test never appears in lcov, so nothing fails; it **skips any test importing vitest** (`:61-64`), and ~4,401 test files import vitest vs ~1,291 `bun:test`, so it covers a minority; threshold is a 50% ratchet.

Net: **nothing requires new code to ship real tests.**

### Vacuous-green holes on the PR hot path

- The runner's `--min-tasks`/`MIN_TEST_TASKS` floors (`packages/scripts/run-all-tests.mjs:256-266,1138,1190`) default to `0` and are set by **no** PR lane (`test`, `test:server`, `test:client`, `test:plugins`, `test:e2e`). So a lane whose tasks all self-skip ("No test files found") exits **green**. The only floor enforcement, `ci-full-matrix-proof.mjs`, uses `--plan=json` (static discovery, never executes tests) and runs twice-daily/narrow-path (`ci-full-matrix-proof.yml:17-32`), off the PR path.
- **`outputIndicatesNoTests` swallows real failures.** `run-all-tests.mjs:359-366` + `:969-972`: any **non-zero** child exit is reclassified as `skipped:true` (→ green) if the last 16 KB of merged stdout+stderr matches `/No test files found/i` / `/did not match any test files/i`. A multi-project vitest / `bun test` run where one project legitimately has no files while another **fails** produces both strings in one buffer → the whole task is marked SKIP=green, hiding the failure. Same pattern in the cloud step (`:1030-1035`).

> The iOS/Android-sim manifestations of this are tracked device-specifically in sibling umbrella #13562 (#13571 "boot-to-error-card passes, whole runs go green with 0 passed", #13572 "test:sim:local-chat passes vacuously when no simulator"). This issue fixes the **general runner mechanism** those lanes rely on.

## Tasks

- [ ] Seed `lint-lane-coverage.allowlist.json` from today's 160 issues (loader already supports it); flip the gate off `--dry-run`; add it to a develop-triggered workflow (`quality.yml`).
- [ ] Extend `coverage-gate.yml` to require a covering test for changed source, and to include vitest tests (or add a vitest coverage lane).
- [ ] Set `MIN_TEST_TASKS`/`--min-tasks` on the real PR lanes (`test`, `test:server`, `test:client`, `test:plugins`, `test:e2e`) with realistic floors.
- [ ] Narrow the "no tests" classification to the runner's own empty-file determination (or an exact-banner match on the whole output), not a substring scan over merged child output.

## Acceptance criteria

- A new surface-bearing plugin with no scenario **reds** on a develop PR; a PR adding untested source **reds**.
- A lane filtered to zero tasks exits **3**, not 0 (extend `run-all-tests-vacuous-green-guard.test.ts`).
- A suite with an empty sub-project **and** a failing test **FAILS** (does not SKIP=green).

## Files

`.github/workflows/ci.yaml`, `quality.yml`, `coverage-gate.yml`, `packages/scripts/run-all-tests.mjs`, `packages/scripts/lint-lane-coverage.mjs` (+ new allowlist), `packages/scripts/__tests__/run-all-tests-vacuous-green-guard.test.ts`.

## Related

Closed #9943 (green-CI≠tested — describes this verbatim), #8801, #12342 (built the min-tasks guard but never armed it on PR lanes). Sibling device lanes: #13571, #13572, #13573.

## Evidence to close ([PR_EVIDENCE.md](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/develop/PR_EVIDENCE.md))

New unit tests + CI logs for each case: the exit-3 demonstration, the empty-project-plus-failure FAIL, a red PR adding untested source, the shrinking coverage allowlist diff.

topIssues.title: Nightly App Live E2E — the only scheduled desktop-packaged lane — is red every night; desktop job fails on screenshot 503 + settings-shell timeout, so the desktop loop has no green unattended cadence
topIssues.author: lalalune
topIssues.body:
Part of the desktop stream of the unattended-testing umbrella #13562. The screenshot-backend half is filed separately (packaged screenshot seam issue); this issue owns making the scheduled lane green.

## Problem

`app-live-e2e.yml` is the only scheduled CI home for the packaged Electrobun desktop suite (`xvfb-run … bun run --cwd packages/app test:desktop:packaged`, line 380) — and it has failed every night for at least three consecutive nights (Jul 1, Jul 2, Jul 3 2026). In the latest completed run **all four jobs failed** (desktop packaged, app live chat, full walkthrough, cloud login+provision+chat). A nightly that is always red is indistinguishable from no lane: nobody is alerted, regressions accumulate silently, and the desktop loop has no unattended green cadence at all.

Desktop-job specifics from run 28647271527 (2026-07-03):

1. `desktop-launch-render.e2e.spec.ts:110` — bridge screenshot 503; the ubuntu runner has none of `scrot`/`import`/`ffmpeg`/`xwd` installed (workflow installs protobuf but no screenshot tool).
2. `electrobun-packaged-regressions.e2e.spec.ts:1030` "packaged desktop persists media, provider, and plugin state across relaunch" — `Timed out waiting for [data-testid="settings-shell"] at /settings/voice` (needs root-cause: renderer routing under WebKitGTK, or live-api server shape drift).
3. Lane summary: 2 failed / 2 skipped / 1 passed — most of the suite is macOS-gated, so the Linux leg exercises very little even when green.

## Evidence

- `gh run list --workflow app-live-e2e.yml`: failure 2026-07-01T08:29Z, cancelled+failure 2026-07-02, failure 2026-07-03T20:48Z (run 28647271527).
- Job log excerpts: `GET http://127.0.0.1:31558/main-window/screenshot failed (503)`, `[ScreenCapture] Executable not found in $PATH: "scrot"|"import"|"ffmpeg"|"xwd"`, `Timed out waiting for [data-testid="settings-shell"] at /settings/voice`, `error: script "test:desktop:packaged" exited with code 1`.
- Artifact `app-live-e2e-desktop` (id 8074563215) uploaded with the failure traces.

## Done when

- The runner provisions at least one Linux screenshot backend (apt `scrot` and/or `ffmpeg`) before the desktop step, or the bridge screenshot no longer needs host CLIs (sibling issue).
- The `/settings/voice` settings-shell timeout is root-caused and fixed (not skipped).
- Three consecutive scheduled runs of the "desktop packaged" job are green, and a red nightly notifies someone (issue comment, Slack, or failing badge referenced from the repo docs).
- The Linux leg's skip list is reviewed: macOS-gated specs that could run under WebKitGTK are un-gated or their skip reason is documented in the workflow.

## Verification

```
gh run list --workflow app-live-e2e.yml --limit 3   # 3 green scheduled runs
gh run view <latest> --json jobs -q '.jobs[] | "\(.conclusion) \(.name)"'
# locally reproduce the Linux leg: xvfb-run -a bun run --cwd packages/app test:desktop:packaged (on a Linux host with scrot installed)
```

topIssues.title: [staging][ops] Staging agents never join headscale — all 48 running agents have empty headscale_ip, so the CP nginx router 404s the worker→CP→agent hop (chat dead-ends after #15205)
topIssues.author: standujar
topIssues.body:
## The layer under #15205
With the CF wildcard + TLS fixed (#15205), the app's per-agent calls now correctly reach `https://<id>.staging.elizacloud.ai` on the STAGING worker (verified: valid `*.staging.elizacloud.ai` cert, request lands on the staging cloud-api worker, no longer the prod one). But the chat still dead-ends: every `/api/*` call returns **HTTP 404 from Cloudflare with no CORS header** → browser reports `No 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin'`.

## Root cause (systemic, not per-agent)
The worker's `handleDedicatedAgentProxy` → `proxyToOrigin` forwards to `AGENT_ROUTER_ORIGIN_HOST = eliza-staging-1.elizacloud.ai` (the staging CP). The CP runs **nginx** (:80/:443) which routes `<id>.staging.elizacloud.ai` to the agent over the **headscale tailnet** via the agent's `headscale_ip`. But:
- **All 48 running staging agents have `headscale_ip` NULL/empty** (`SELECT (headscale_ip IS NULL OR headscale_ip='') , count(*) FROM agent_sandboxes WHERE status='running'` → `t | 48`).
- **`headscale nodes list` on the CP shows NO online agent-tagged node** — only `cp-staging-router` (tag:eliza-proxy, online) and two `robot-tstest`/`robot-tstest2` (tag:agent) **offline since 2026-06-16**.

So staging agent containers are provisioned + running + serving on their node bridge (`bridge_url` is set, e.g. `http://91.98.38.74:19006`), but they **never join the headscale mesh**, so the CP router has no tailnet address to reach them → 404. The agent's own CORS (`resolveCorsOrigin`, which allows any origin when `ELIZA_CLOUD_PROVISIONED=1`) is never reached because the request dies at the CP hop.

## Why it surfaced only now
Nobody ever got a staging agent reachable end-to-end before tonight (DB split #15160 → image boot #15196 → wildcard/TLS #15205 all had to land first). This is the next distinct gap in the same 'staging never fully mirrored prod' class, adjacent to the known prod-parity headscale gap.

## What to investigate
Why staging agent containers don't join headscale: is the tailscale-up / headscale pre-auth-key step injected at provision time (the staging worker HAS `HEADSCALE_PUBLIC_URL`/`HEADSCALE_API_URL`/`HEADSCALE_USER=tunnel`) actually running in the container, and is the provisioning worker recording `headscale_ip` back to `agent_sandboxes`? Either the join is failing/skipped or the IP is never persisted. Fixing it should light up all 48 agents at once.

## Scope
Systemic (48/48 agents), needs the headscale/tailnet provisioning path debugged — an infra workstream, not a config toggle. #15205's edge routing is done and verified; this is the CP→agent hop. [stan-cloud]

topIssues.title: [onboarding] P0 — Resurrect App Live E2E: real cloud login + real-LLM chat must produce a green nightly run
topIssues.author: lalalune
topIssues.body:
## Problem
The only tests proving that a REAL Eliza Cloud account works and a REAL LLM answers after onboarding live in the nightly `App Live E2E` workflow — and that workflow has produced no green scheduled run since at least 2026-06-25 (every run 06-25→07-05 is `failure` or `cancelled`). The production-default onboarding is therefore unverified end to end.

## Current state (file refs)
- Workflow: `.github/workflows/app-live-e2e.yml` (nightly 07:00 UTC + dispatch; `ELIZA_UI_SMOKE_LIVE_STACK=1` un-forces the CI stub).
- Live specs it runs: `packages/app/test/ui-smoke/cloud-live.spec.ts` (real login via `ELIZAOS_CLOUD_API_KEY`, real provisioning, real cloud chat turn asserting the reply does NOT contain `STUB_FIXTURE_MARKER`) and `packages/app/test/ui-smoke/live-agent-chat.spec.ts` (real local runtime + live provider).
- Known long-standing failure modes (pre-existing): (1) `desktop packaged` job dies in `packages/app-core/scripts/copy-runtime-node-modules.ts` (`71 required runtime package check(s) failed after copy + prune` — every `@elizaos/plugin-*` missing `dist/node_modules/.../dist/index.js`); (2) `app live chat` job times out at `live-agent-chat.spec.ts` "sends a message to the live agent and renders the response" (`toBeVisible()` not found after ~2.1m).

## Proposed change
1. Triage each red job independently — they are unrelated failures. Fix the runtime-copy prune/filter bug (or build plugin dists before the copy) for the desktop-packaged job; debug the live chat turn (provider selection, model boot, stream render) for the live-chat job.
2. Do NOT weaken assertions or add mocks to go green — the lane exists to be real.
3. If a sub-job is genuinely out of MVP scope (e.g. desktop packaged build), split it into its own job so cloud-live can pass independently; keep it visible, never delete coverage silently.
4. Trigger a `workflow_dispatch` run after the fix and confirm green.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] One fully green scheduled or dispatched `App Live E2E` run on `develop`, linked in the PR.
- [ ] `cloud-live.spec.ts` passes against real Eliza Cloud: real session, real provisioning, real chat turn, non-stub reply asserted.
- [ ] `live-agent-chat.spec.ts` passes with a real provider model turn rendered in the UI.
- [ ] No assertion was weakened and no network mock was added to any live spec (diff review).
- [ ] Root cause of each failure documented in the PR body (not just "fixed").

## Evidence required (posted INLINE in the PR)
- Link to the green workflow run.
- MP4 of the Playwright trace/video for the cloud-live spec (real login → onboarded → real reply visible).
- JPG screenshots: the WRONG behavior first (red run log excerpt), then the passing chat turn with the real model reply.
- Server + client log excerpts showing the real cloud request/response (redact tokens) in a collapsed details block.

---
_Workstream: **Onboarding, tutorial & help** · [design doc](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/develop/packages/docs/ongoing-development/research/04-onboarding-tutorial-help.md) · [MVP board](https://github.com/orgs/elizaOS/projects/15)_

topIssues.title: fix(observability): make chat latency telemetry truthful and correlate every hop end to end
topIssues.author: NubsCarson
topIssues.body:
## Problem

We cannot currently explain a slow chat turn from one correlated production trace.

The live `X-Eliza-Preforward-Ms` header is also semantically incorrect. The structured log freezes `totalMs` before provider dispatch, but the response header recomputes it after awaiting the streaming handler, which already waited for the provider response. It therefore includes provider-to-headers time while claiming to represent only pre-forward work. Outer Hono/global rate-limit work is not included at all.

This produced incorrect conclusions such as attributing a 6.8s Gemma first-token result entirely to gateway pre-forward work.

## Required trace

Mint one bounded, validated trace ID and propagate it through:

browser → dedicated proxy → agent route → plugin runtime → Cloud API Worker → Cerebras request → first reasoning/content frame → stream completion

Record monotonic boundaries for:

- browser dispatch, response headers, first SSE event, first reasoning delta, first visible content, `[DONE]`
- global limiter and route/API-key limiter
- auth KV/cache and authoritative auth
- organization lookup and organization limiter
- app authorization, credential pool, catalog/pricing, moderation, balance/admission
- provider fetch start, response headers, first upstream frame, first reasoning delta, first content delta, stream completion
- background billing settlement separately from user-visible response time
- Cloudflare colo and `cf-placement`

Do not log prompts, API keys, authorization headers, or unbounded attacker-controlled identifiers.

## Persistence

- Enable sampled Workers traces with custom spans.
- Write aggregate latency events to Workers Analytics Engine.
- Preserve app trace IDs because Cloudflare native trace context is not propagated to external providers.
- Store provider completion/request IDs where Cerebras exposes them.
- Poll Cerebras organization metrics for queue time, TTFT, TPOT, cache rate, and end-to-end latency.

## Benchmark harness

The harness must:

- randomize model and direct/gateway ordering
- use the same prompt, effective token budget, reasoning controls, credential/service tier, and client region
- distinguish cold, warm, and post-idle requests
- collect at least 30 samples per model/path
- report p50/p90/p95 for headers, first event, first visible token, and completion
- retain redacted JSON evidence tied to deployed Worker version

## Acceptance

- The pre-forward header is frozen before provider dispatch and agrees with the corresponding structured event.
- Outer middleware timings are visible instead of disappearing before the route timer starts.
- A single trace can be followed across browser, dedicated agent, plugin, gateway, and provider-facing boundaries.
- First SSE, first reasoning, and first visible content remain separate metrics.
- Staging proof includes Gemma and GLM-4.7, direct and gateway, cold and warm.
- Existing streaming, CORS, billing, abort, and no-prompt-logging tests remain green.

## References

- Cloudflare Workers traces and custom spans:
  https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/observability/traces/
- Cloudflare tracing limitation for external services:
  https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/observability/traces/known-limitations/
- Analytics Engine writes are nonblocking:
  https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/observability/metrics-and-analytics/
- Cerebras organization latency metrics:
  https://inference-docs.cerebras.ai/api-reference/metrics/retrieve-metrics
- Historical pre-forward instrumentation: #9909
- Gateway latency tracker: #15428

topPRs.title: release: promote develop → production (money-integrity wave, monetization rails, auth overhaul, live rate limiting)
topPRs.author: NubsCarson
topPRs.body:
## Production promote: develop → main (444 commits)

Prod has been running a **manually-promoted develop frontend** (`d2b8782`, via local `wrangler pages deploy`) against a **day-old Worker and schema** since ~00:00Z — any main push regresses the frontend; the skew only grows. This PR makes prod durable and lockstep: merging triggers `cloud-deploy-backend` (migrate-db) **and** `cloud-cf-deploy` (Worker `--env production`, both Pages `--branch=main`) from the same main push.

Full runbook: `PROD_PROMOTE_RUNBOOK.md` in the deploy-lane worktree + condensed in elizaOS/eliza#10561 (comment 4862165568). Analysis: 4-agent delta/hazard/mechanics/validation pass over `main..develop`.

### Pre-merge checklist (why this is DRAFT)
- [x] **REDIS_URL present in prod Worker env** — verified 2026-07-02 ~05:50Z via `wrangler secret list --env production` (223 secrets; REDIS_URL + MCP cache Redis present). The #10620 fail-closed rate-limit guard will pass. (Presence-verified; a dead URL degrades to fail-open limiting, not an outage.)
- [x] develop merges into main clean (`git merge-tree --write-tree`: no conflicts; the 2 main-only CodeQL commits reconcile with their develop-parity equivalents)
- [x] Staging validated on this code lineage (sign-in renders, onboarding renders, 0 CORS, API health ok — #10561 00:55Z + 01:55Z evidence)
- [ ] **Deploy window**: robots take ONE deploy at a time (#11108). At merge time, hold develop deploy runs until the main run completes (the cloud/laptop agent session runs the escort and will cover this — ping in #10561).
- [ ] **Watch `migrate-db` go green** on the main push (cloud-deploy-backend). If it fails, the Worker still ships → roll the Worker back (re-dispatch env=production from `23f33ccc`) or hotfix the DB before traffic notices.
- [ ] Post-deploy validation: automated harness (bundle-hash flip, 5 sign-in options render, 0 CORS, `api/health` ok) + the 2-minute real sign-in → message → credits-deduct manual pass. Abort/rollback signals in the runbook (Pages = CF dashboard rollback, proven 06-25).

### What ships (headlines)
- **Money-integrity wave**: creator-earnings idempotency across all money routes; 3 payout double-pay windows closed; Stripe refund/chargeback clawbacks (non-negative); atomic crypto top-up; upfront credit reservation vs `max_tokens`; org-credit gates on agent resume; per-app API key scoping; per-org agent/container caps. Zero-balance orgs start getting **correct rejections** — visible behavior change.
- **Monetization rails**: miniapp Stripe/OxaPay credit rails + compliance-review gate + admin-approved USDC payouts; ad SSP; influencer marketplace w/ escrow; managed frontend hosting; agent-driven custom domains.
- **Auth/onboarding overhaul**: apex lands authed users on the console (#11031, already hand-promoted); same-origin API proxy; OAuth redirect + Suspense crash + session-loop fixes; apex-401 root fix (#11004); reworked first-run onboarding; pre-auth polling gated (#11084).
- **Rate limiting goes live** in prod (#10620) — pre-check above clears the fail-closed guard.
- Optional secrets degrade gracefully if unset: `OXAPAY_MERCHANT_API_KEY`, `ELIZA_AD_TAG_SECRET`, `ELIZA_FRONTEND_HOST_SUFFIX`, `APP_REVIEW_MODEL`. `FAL_KEY` is present-but-invalid (#11005) — independent ops fix, not gated on this PR.

### Migrations
9 additive migrations (0155–0163: withdrawal idempotency, frontend hosting, compliance gate w/ backfill, influencer + ad tables, domains anti-squat unique swap). Auto-applied by migrate-db on the main push; old code ignores the new tables, so a code rollback needs no schema rollback.

**Draft until @NubsCarson + @lalalune call it.** Merging this = production deploy.
